items.title: Backlog capture: every fenced code block on the site carries empty line-anchor links, each one an invisible keyboard Tab stop
items.body: Backlog capture: every fenced code block on the site carries empty line-anchor links, each one an invisible keyboard Tab stop. Found during the M19-R7 end-to-end check (#53). `zensical.toml` sets `[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.highlight] anchor_linenums = true`, but no block shows line numbers, so each code line gets an `` with no content: zero width, no visible focus ring, and still in the tab order. What I saw (built from `main` at aaf83cf with `SYNC_SOURCE_BASE=/home/darren/projects/radiusred`): counting `href="#__codelineno` in the built pages gives 77 on `site/docs/cli/index.html`, 72 on `first-milestone`, 62 on `extensions`, 43 on `spec`, 14 on `platform-interop`, 12 on `working-offline`, 11 on the docs index and 2 on `identities`; each is a Tab stop a keyboard user cannot see. On the homepage the routing example had 18 of them in a row, between the block's copy button and the next link. #53 handles the homepage only, with `.md-typeset .cc-crew .highlight a[id^="__codelineno-"] { visibility: hidden; }`, because the task keeps docs and blog pages unchanged. The site-wide options are `anchor_linenums = false` (loses nothing visible, since no block shows line numbers, but breaks any deep link to `#__codelineno-…`) or the same `visibility: hidden` rule without the homepage scope.

items.title: Thesis Weeks 4–18
items.body:
Thesis Guide¶

Step 5 of 5 in the Deliverables section. You should have your presentation ready from the previous step. Now it is time to compile and finalize your thesis documentation.

TL;DR

Your thesis is a set of Markdown files that you convert to PDF. Download the template, fill in each section with content about your project, generate the PDF, and submit it in a ZIP archive. Total length: 32,000–51,500 characters (~17–25 A4 pages).

What Is This¶

Your project documentation is a technical document describing your diploma project in an industry-standard format. This is not an academic essay — it is a real document that could be used in an IT company: problem description, architectural decisions, user manual, and honest analysis of results.

Format: Markdown (.md files) → PDF

Why Markdown:

  • Stored in Git alongside your code
  • Easy to edit and version control
  • Works well with AI assistants
  • Automatic PDF generation

Template¶

Download template: [GitHub repository link]

The template has a ready-made folder structure and files with placeholders. Fill them with your content.

Document Structure¶

docs/
├── index.md                    # Title page
├── 01-project-overview/        # Section 1: Project Overview (BA)
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── problem-and-goals.md
│   ├── stakeholders.md
│   ├── scope.md
│   └── features.md
├── 02-technical/               # Section 2: Technical Implementation
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── tech-stack.md
│   ├── criteria/               # Your 7 evaluation criteria
│   │   ├── [criterion-1].md
│   │   ├── [criterion-2].md
│   │   └── ...
│   └── deployment.md
├── 03-user-guide/              # Section 3: User Guide
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── features.md
│   └── faq.md
├── 04-retrospective/           # Section 4: Retrospective
│   └── index.md
└── assets/                     # Images and diagrams
    └── images/

Step-by-Step Workflow¶

Step 1: Preparation¶

  1. Download the template from GitHub
  2. Create your own repository or folder for documentation
  3. Copy the template structure
  4. Install PDF generation tools (see "PDF Generation" below)

Step 2: Title page¶

Fill in index.md:

  • Project name
  • Your details (full name, group, supervisor)
  • Links to production, repository, Figma
  • List of selected evaluation criteria

Step 3: Project overview¶

Fill in the 01-project-overview/ section:

File | What to write -- | -- index.md | Executive summary, links problem-and-goals.md | Problem, user pain points, goals and KPIs stakeholders.md | Target audience, personas scope.md | In/Out scope, constraints, assumptions features.md | Epics, user stories, use case diagram

File naming

  • Use Latin characters: Ivanov_Ivan_Diploma.zip
  • No spaces — use _ or -
  • Last name first

Pre-Submission Checklist¶

Documentation¶

  • All template sections are filled in
  • No placeholders like [Name] or [description]
  • All links work
  • Images display correctly
  • PDF is generated and readable
  • All 7 evaluation criteria are listed
  • Technical criteria include diagrams (architecture, component, ER, sequence, or deployment diagrams)
  • Diagrams are original (created for your project, not generic examples)

Code¶

  • Each repository in a separate ZIP
  • README with run instructions exists
  • No secrets in code (passwords, API keys)
  • .env.example is present
  • Code runs successfully

General¶

  • Archive structure matches the format above
  • Files are named correctly
  • Archive opens without errors

items.title: Review duplicate generated source-line IDs in mesh API reference
items.body:
The mesh API reference published by #459 has unique API/heading anchors, but multiple expandable source blocks from GeomMeshDataclasses produce duplicate generated line IDs (for example `__span-0-60` and `__codelineno-0-60`). The local final strict build detected 52 duplicated source-line identifiers on this page; strict MkDocs validation does not flag them. The production page also passes the API/heading anchor checks.

Please review mkdocstrings/Pymdown source rendering so each source snippet gets a unique line-ID prefix without removing source visibility or breaking public API anchors. This is a renderer/navigation follow-up, not a hydraulic or API execution defect.

Acceptance criteria:
- No repeated IDs within the generated mesh reference page.
- Expandable source code, syntax highlighting and API signature rendering remain usable.
- Public method and result-class anchor URLs remain stable.
- Verify on the built HTML, not just Markdown or a successful strict build.

Page: https://rascommander.info/ras/api/rasmapper/mesh-generation/

items.title: Anchor validation false positives after upgrading to 1.6
items.body:
First of all, thanks for the very useful [new anchor validation feature](https://www.mkdocs.org/about/release-notes/#anchors)! Upgrading to MkDocs 1.6, I was able to [fix many stale anchors in our documentation](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/7076#issuecomment-2076300125). However, in the process, I came across a few false positives – the anchors are correct, but MkDocs reports them nonetheless. This is particularly the case when using the [Tabbed](https://facelessuser.github.io/pymdown-extensions/extensions/tabbed/) extension with [`combine_header_slug`](https://facelessuser.github.io/pymdown-extensions/extensions/tabbed/#tab-ids), which allows to prepend the slug of the nearest header to the tab.

I believe this needs to be fixed in MkDocs, since it might be some kind of ordering issue when running anchor validation, but I'm tagging @facelessuser here for visibility. By using the [Tabbed](https://facelessuser.github.io/pymdown-extensions/extensions/tabbed/) extension, anchor links to tabs are much more readable, something that many users asked for on the Material for MkDocs issue tracker.

## Example

The following example is used for illustration. You can also download it here: [anchor-validation-bug.zip](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/files/15144456/anchor-validation-bug.zip)

`index.md`

``` markdown
# Page with tabs

## Headline

=== "Tab A"

    Anchor for this tab is `#headline-tab-a`

=== "Tab B"

    Anchor for this tab is `#headline-tab-b`
```

`foo.md`

``` markdown
# Links to tabs

- [Tab A](index.md#headline-tab-a)
- [Tab B](index.md#headline-tab-b)
```

MkDocs will not detect those links and report them as non-existent:

```
INFO    -  Cleaning site directory
INFO    -  Doc file 'foo.md' contains a link 'index.md#headline-tab-a', but the doc 'index.md' does not contain an anchor '#headline-tab-a'.
INFO    -  Doc file 'foo.md' contains a link 'index.md#headline-tab-b', but the doc 'index.md' does not contain an anchor '#headline-tab-b'.
INFO    -  Documentation built in 0.12 seconds
```

When running the example, it's easy to see that anchor are correct and work as expected.

items.title: the homepage's metadata matches the pitch, and the page reads cleanly everywhere

labels.name: cc:task
labels.description: CodeCrew: a task issue, attached to its milestone as a sub-issue (SPEC §4)

items.body:
## Goal
Once R2–R6 have landed, the frontmatter still carries the receipts-led description. Set homepage-only metadata to match the new pitch, and check the rebuilt page end to end: 375px and 1280px, light and dark, keyboard focus, the mobile drawer, and docs and blog pages unchanged. Fix what the check finds on the homepage.

## Requirements
M19-R7

## Plan
Covers **M19-R7**. The last task before QA: R1–R6 have landed, and their Decisions are read.

**1. Homepage metadata, for the homepage only.**
- `docs/index.md` frontmatter: a new `description` in the new pitch (agents under their own GitHub App identities, different harnesses and models building and reviewing each other's work, the record in GitHub), replacing the receipts-led one. It feeds `<meta name="description">`, `og:description` and `twitter:description`.
- The homepage's `<title>`, `og:title` and `twitter:title` are `CodeCrew — ` plus main.html's receipts-led tagline, because the page's title is the site name. `docs/overrides/home.html` overrides the `htmltitle` and `extrahead` blocks to set that tagline from a `tagline` key in the homepage's frontmatter, then renders the parent block, so the head markup stays in main.html. `zensical.toml`'s `site_description` and main.html's default tagline stay as they are (404 and the docs keep them).
- Test first: a build test pins the homepage's emitted description (all three tags) and title (all three), and that a docs page and a blog post keep theirs.

**2. The end-to-end check** (Playwright, headless Chromium): the full homepage at 375px and 1280px, light and dark; document scrollWidth against the viewport; every section read; a Tab walk (visible focus ring, no invisible stops, no trap); the drawer opened and closed at 375px; the hero headline above the fold at 375px. Then the built docs and blog pages diffed against a build of `c23ea93^` (before M19).

Found in a first pass, to fix on the homepage (homepage-scoped CSS/markup, each recorded as a Decision with before/after):
- the logo is 260px wide at 375px, so the pitch starts halfway down the first screen: shrink it on narrow viewports;
- the illustrative `roles:` YAML (354px in a 328px box) and the install terminal (366px in 326px) scroll sideways at 375px, and so each becomes a focus stop: fit them;
- the YAML block carries 18 zero-width line anchors (`#__codelineno-0-N`, from the site-wide `anchor_linenums`), each an invisible Tab stop: take them out of the homepage's tab order;
- the example's name lines break `radiusred-` / `cody[bot]` at 375px: keep the App login whole.

Anything real outside the homepage becomes an unlabeled "Backlog capture:" issue, not a fix (first pass: the same zero-width line anchors on every docs page with a code block; the phone drawer's links taking focus while the drawer is closed, on every page).

**3. Tests** ride with it: the metadata test above, plus build tests for the CSS the fixes add where a build test can see it.

Files: `docs/index.md`, `docs/overrides/home.html`, `docs/stylesheets/extra.css` (`.cc-*` only), `tests/test_site_build.py`.

## Ask-the-human points
None. The operator's check of the rendered page before the record is the milestone's own gate, after QA.

items.title: docs: the homepage's metadata carries the crew pitch, and the page reads cleanly everywhere (#53)
items.body:
Closes #53

Covers **M19-R7**: the homepage's metadata carries the new pitch, on the homepage only, and the rebuilt page was checked end to end at 375px and 1280px, light and dark, with the keyboard and the phone drawer, with docs and blog pages compared against a pre-M19 build. The last M19 task before QA.

## What changed

**Metadata (homepage only).** `docs/index.md`'s front matter: `description` is now "Give each coding agent its own GitHub App identity, so different harnesses and models can build and review each other's work, with the record kept in GitHub." and a new `tagline` is "Your coding agents, working as a crew on GitHub" (the hero headline). `docs/overrides/home.html` overrides `htmltitle` and `extrahead` only to set main.html's `tagline` from the page, then renders the parent block. Emitted on the homepage: `<title>`, `og:title`, `twitter:title` = "CodeCrew — Your coding agents, working as a crew on GitHub"; `<meta name="description">`, `og:description`, `twitter:description` = the new description. `zensical.toml` and main.html are untouched. [Decision](https://github.com/radiusred/codecrew-www/issues/53#issuecomment-5842323529)

What the check turned up on the homepage, and what changed (homepage-scoped CSS/markup, each with before/after in its Decision):

- **Code blocks at 375px**: the install terminal (366px of content in a 326px box) and the routing YAML (354 in 328, last row clipped at "operato") scrolled sideways. Below 420px both step down from 12.8px to 11.2px: now 322 in 322 and 328 in 328. [Decision](https://github.com/radiusred/codecrew-www/issues/53#issuecomment-5842332904)
- **18 invisible Tab stops**: the YAML's empty `__codelineno` line anchors (site-wide `anchor_linenums`) are now `visibility: hidden` under `.cc-crew .highlight`. [Decision](https://github.com/radiusred/codecrew-www/issues/53#issuecomment-5842336526)
- **Logo on phones**: 13rem → 7rem below 45em. At 375x667 the headline moves from 376–501px to 256–381px and the first hero paragraph now ends at 629px, above the fold; the buttons end at 1006px (was 1126), still below it. [Decision](https://github.com/radiusred/codecrew-www/issues/53#issuecomment-5842340045)
- **App logins in the example**: "radiusred-" / "cody[bot]" broke at the hyphen at 375px; a `nowrap` span keeps each login whole. [Decision](https://github.com/radiusred/codecrew-www/issues/53#issuecomment-5842349724)

Tests: `test_home_metadata_carries_the_crew_pitch` and `test_the_home_metadata_stays_on_the_home_page` (docs page, 404 and newest blog post keep their title and description) landed first and failed on `main`; plus one test for each CSS change, and R3's who-line test now checks the login span. 82 passed.

## Evidence

Headless Chromium (Playwright, chromium 1243), `site/` served locally, color scheme set with `prefers-color-scheme`. Screenshots are in the dispatch directory, not committed.

| Viewport × theme | Scheme on body | Document scrollWidth | Horizontal overflow | Scrolling blocks | Hero headline (px from top) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 375 × light | default | 360 (viewport 375) | none | none (was 2) | 256–381, above the 667 fold |
| 375 × dark | slate | 360 (viewport 375) | none | none (was 2) | 256–381, above the 667 fold |
| 1280 × light | default | 1265 (viewport 1280) | none | none | 144–250 |
| 1280 × dark | slate | 1265 (viewport 1280) | none | none | 144–250 |

No element inside the homepage content extends past the viewport in any of the four. Every section was read in full-page captures at all four; the proof screenshots load when scrolled to (they are lazy-loaded).

**Focus walk** (Tab from the top until focus repeats): stops inside the homepage content went 45 → 25 at 375px and 43 → 25 at 1280px (the 18 line anchors, plus the two scrolling code blocks at 375px). All 25 have a non-zero box and a computed focus outline; captures at 375px, light and dark, show the ring on the hero link, both hero buttons, the YAML copy button, a proof link, a receipt link, a terminal copy button and a Start now link. No trap: focus runs through the footer's social links and leaves the content. Two theme-level things remain on every page, not only this one: at 375px the drawer's links take focus off-screen while it is shut (captured as #58), and after the last footer link Chromium lands on an empty, classless `div` with `position: fixed` for three presses, on docs and blog pages too, before reaching the body; I could not tell whether that is the theme or the headless browser, so I have not captured it.

**Drawer at 375px** (light and dark): the burger opens it (`#__drawer` checked, sidebar at left 8px, Home, Docs with its pages, Blog with its posts all visible); a tap on the overlay shuts it (unchecked, sidebar back at -242px). The home template still emits the hidden `md-sidebar--primary`, pinned by the existing drawer tests.

**Docs and blog unchanged.** Built `c23ea93^` (80c0c94, before the first M19 change) and this branch the same way, then `diff -rq` the two `site/` trees: only `index.html`, `search.json` (only the homepage's entries; all 128 other entries identical), `stylesheets/extra.css` (every added or removed selector is a `.cc-*` one, and all 14 non-`.cc` rules are byte-identical) and the copied `overrides/home.html` template differ. Every other page is byte-identical, including `docs/index.html` and both blog posts. Full-page captures of `/docs/`, `/docs/identities/`, `/docs/cli/`, `/blog/`, the newest post and `/404.html`, at 375 and 1280, light and dark, are pixel-identical between the two builds.

## Backlog captures (outside the homepage, not changed here)

- #57: the same empty line anchors on every docs page with a code block (77 on the CLI reference).
- #58: on phones the drawer's links take keyboard focus off-screen while it is shut, on every page.
- #59: the docs pages and the 404 still carry the receipts-led site description and tagline; whether they should follow the homepage is the operator's call.

## For the reviewer

- The title change goes beyond the `description` the task names: the old title was the other half of the receipts-led pitch. It is homepage-only; the 404, whose title is also the site name, keeps main.html's tagline (pinned).
- `home.html` relies on a block-local `set` being visible to `super()` in MiniJinja. That was checked in the build (a top-level `set` is overwritten by main.html's own) and is pinned by the metadata test, so a Zensical upgrade that changes it fails CI.
- At 360px the install terminal still runs 11px over; the requirement names 375px (see the code-size Decision).
- No copy changed apart from the front matter; the example's who lines gained a span but read the same.
